title: Adaptive prefetch handshake to prevent mixed-length queue starvation across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Menon
description: Multiple customer escalations (hosted and private clusters) exposed a recurring pattern: mixed-length workloads with long-context requests were causing intermittent queue starvation for short/latency-sensitive requests. Root cause analysis points to two interacting phenomena: (1) KV cache prefetches and eviction handoffs create bursty backend work that inflates admission windows, and (2) the continuous batching admission logic lacks a lightweight handshake to signal when a slot includes long-context KV warming. The result: short requests get delayed behind batches being held open for KV prewarm, amplifying P99 tail latency for small requests and triggering customer-facing timeouts in Dedicated and Private deployments. This ticket implements an "adaptive prefetch handshake" plus admission smoothing to ensure short flows are protected while preserving batching efficiency for long requests.
updates: 2026-02-12 - Ticket created after PagerDuty escalation from Acme Health (private) and two Hosted customers reporting 5-15s P99 spikes for short requests during mixed-length bursts.

2026-02-13 - Reproduced locally with mixed replay harness (10% long-context 20% medium 70% short) using runtime-1.19 config. Observed KV prefetch spikes correlate with scheduler admission window growth; captured flamegraphs and KV cache metrics (prefetch_latency, eviction_rate).

2026-02-17 - Spike root cause hypothesis: prefetch-triggered work extends batch assembly time; admission window increases to maintain throughput, causing head-of-line blocking for short requests. Created simulation to test admitting handshake token that marks batch as 'warming'.

2026-02-20 - Prototype: admission handshake implemented in the continuous-batcher: an optional prefetch token with tight timeout (ms) that defers full KV handoff to a background prewarm path. Local simulation shows 40% reduction in short-request P99 in mixed mix at 2% extra CPU.

2026-02-25 - Design review with PM and runtime team. Trade-offs discussed: extra scheduling state per batch vs. reduction in tail; agreed on opt-in rollout controlled by per-deployment feature flag and a per-tenant fairness floor.

2026-03-01 - Implemented end-to-end patch (scheduler: adaptive_prefetch_handshake + admission_smoothing). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892. Added metrics: handshake_latency, handshake_missed, warm_background_success.
2026-03-04 - Integration test against Dedicated staging cluster passed. Added canary config (5% of traffic) with thresholds: P99 short < 1200ms and handshake_missed < 1% over 5m.

2026-03-07 - Canary rollout to Hosted prod (canary group) triggered. Observed immediate P99 improvement for short requests; long-request throughput unchanged within 2% margin. Two customer support cases closed.

2026-03-09 - Small regression: under very high long-request-only load, background prewarm increased memory pressure on certain Private nodes. Mitigation: cap background prewarm concurrency per node and add eviction backpressure.
2026-03-10 - Patch updated to include node-level prewarm cap and eviction backpressure. Preparing for broader rollout after one more week of monitoring and an on-call runbook.
2026-03-10 - Next steps: finalize rollout playbook, update console metrics dashboards, schedule post-deploy smoke window, and write short postmortem for escalations.
acceptance_criteria: Short-request P99 improves by at least 30% under mixed-length replay compared to baseline without handshake
Long-request throughput (tokens/s) within ±5% of baseline in sustained runs
Handshake_missed rate < 1% for canary traffic and < 2% for broad rollout
No unbounded memory growth in Private clusters; node-level prewarm cap enforced
Rollout runbook created and on-call engineers trained
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature-flagged deploy to staging clusters (done)
Phase 2: Canary on Hosted (5% traffic) with 24h observation (done)
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% with automated rollback on metric breach (next)
Phase 4: Dedicated and Private opt-in customers invited to enable via console for 2-week evaluation
Phase 5: Full rollout after 7-day stability window
mitigations: Short-term: Temporary ingress rate caps and per-tenant short-request priority rules applied to affected customers
Long-term: Scheduler refactor to expose admission-weight hints to load balancer and autoscaler
